paragraphs.title: God’s Salvation Revealed Before the Nations

easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “O sing unto the LORD a new song.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist command people to sing unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The LORD has made known His salvation.
easy.q: What has the LORD made known?

answers: All the ends of the earth
easy.explanation: The verse says, “all the ends of the earth have seen the salvation of our God.”
easy.q: Who has seen the salvation of God?

answers: Because the LORD has done marvellous things and brought salvation
medium.explanation: The new song responds to the marvellous things and victory accomplished by the LORD.
medium.q: Why is a new song being sung?

medium.explanation: The LORD openly showed His righteousness before the heathen, meaning He clearly revealed it.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “openly shewed” mean?

answers: His remembrance of them is followed by all the earth seeing His salvation
They keep the nations from seeing salvation
They cause the song to stop
medium.explanation: The psalm says that the LORD remembered His mercy and truth toward Israel, and then all the ends of the earth saw His salvation.
medium.q: How are the LORD’s mercy and truth toward Israel connected with the salvation seen by the earth?

answers: God’s salvation concerns the whole world, not Israel alone
God’s salvation belongs only to the heathen
Israel has no connection with salvation
challenge.explanation: The passage joins God’s faithfulness to Israel with salvation being seen throughout the earth.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by salvation being revealed before the heathen and seen by all the earth?

answers: The LORD’s wonders and victory lead to His righteousness and salvation being revealed to the world
The verses describe three unrelated subjects
The song ends before salvation is mentioned
challenge.explanation: The marvellous works in verse 1 are followed by the revelation of salvation and righteousness before the nations.
challenge.q: What connection exists between verse 1 and verses 2–3?

answers: The LORD’s power by which He gained the victory
The boundaries of the sea and mountains
challenge.explanation: The LORD’s right hand and holy arm are poetic descriptions of His saving power.
challenge.q: What do “his right hand” and “his holy arm” represent in this passage?

paragraphs.title: The World Sings with Musical Instruments

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Make a joyful noise unto the LORD, all the earth.”
easy.q: Who is called to make a joyful noise unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The psalm commands, “Sing unto the LORD with the harp.”
easy.q: Which instrument is named for singing unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: The passage mentions trumpets and the sound of a cornet.
easy.q: Which additional instruments are mentioned for making a joyful noise?

answers: A joyful noise, rejoicing and singing, harp music, then trumpets and a cornet
medium.explanation: The verses progress from joyful shouting and singing to harp music and then trumpets and a cornet.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the call to worship in these verses?

answers: Praise expressed with energetic, audible celebration
A command to hide the voice
medium.explanation: In context, “make a loud noise” describes vigorous praise and rejoicing before the LORD.
medium.q: In this passage, what does “make a loud noise” communicate?

answers: Many voices and different instruments join together
medium.explanation: The passage includes joyful noise, singing, a harp, trumpets, and a cornet.
medium.q: Why does the worship sound increasingly powerful?

answers: It is intended for the whole world, not merely a small group
It is intended only for musicians
It belongs only to one location
challenge.explanation: The command is addressed to “all the earth,” showing that the praise is universal.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “all the earth” teach about the scope of the praise?

answers: The music is offered before the LORD in recognition of His kingship
The music is only for entertainment
The music is directed toward the sea
challenge.explanation: The instruments and joyful noise are made before the LORD, who is identified as the King.
challenge.q: How does the title “the LORD, the King” affect the meaning of the music?

answers: “Rejoice, and sing praise” together with the harp, trumpets, and cornet
Only the words “the sea” and “the world”
challenge.explanation: The verses combine vocal praise with several musical instruments.
challenge.q: Which detail shows that the praise includes both human voices and instruments?

paragraphs.title: All Nature Rejoices Before God’s Judgment

answers: The sea, the world, the floods, and the hills
easy.explanation: The verses mention the sea, the world, the floods, and the hills.
easy.q: Which parts of creation are called to join the praise?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Let the floods clap their hands.”
easy.q: What do the floods do in the psalm’s poetic description?

easy.explanation: The psalm says, “he cometh to judge the earth.”

medium.explanation: “With equity” describes judging the people fairly and uprightly.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “with equity” mean?

answers: Because He comes to judge the earth righteously and the people fairly
Because the sea has stopped roaring
medium.explanation: The rejoicing is connected with the LORD’s righteous judgment.
medium.q: Why does all nature rejoice before the LORD?

answers: As actively joining the universal song
medium.explanation: The sea roars, the floods clap their hands, and the hills are joyful together.
medium.q: How are the sea, the floods, and the hills portrayed?

answers: Personification: nature is given actions such as roaring, clapping, and rejoicing
A description of weapons of war
challenge.explanation: The floods and hills are described as though they can clap and rejoice.
challenge.q: What literary device is especially noticeable in the description of nature?

answers: Both humanity and creation participate in the praise before the LORD
Only nature participates while everyone else is silent
Nature appears without any connection to judgment
challenge.explanation: The sea, world, floods, and hills join the universal praise before the LORD judges the earth and the people.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “all the earth” in verse 9 and nature in verses 7–8?

answers: The LORD’s judgment reaches the whole world and is carried out with righteousness and equity
The judgment applies only to the sea
challenge.explanation: The final verse says that the LORD will judge the world with righteousness and the people with equity.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the judgment of the world and the people?
